simSpeed.value: Sim speed is set to SIM_SPEED.

screenButtonsHelpText.value: Explore bound states across multiple, modifiable single well potentials.

energyDiagram.value:
In the Energy Diagram, observe the energy level structure of the chosen potential well.
Modify each potential well shape and explore the changes to the bound state energy levels. 
Change the potential well type to explore different shapes. You can also change the mass of the system.

quantumStateGraph.value:
In the Quantum State Graph, you can observe the probability density or wave function for
the selected energy level. If viewing
the wave function, you can toggle parts of the graph, such as the real or imaginary part.
There is also an option to show the magnitude and, if enabled, the phase of the wave function.

controlArea.value:
There are a few controls for visual inspection of the energy diagram or controlling the speed
of the simulation. Toggle the visual labels on the energy diagram. Add a reference line to 
visually compare the probability density or wave function to the boundaries of the potential
well. A magnifier can aid in telling apart closely spaced energy levels. You can track the
time the system has been evolving or hide it. There are controls to pause, step through, or 
restart the system. For slowly evolving states, you can increase the sim speed.

interactionHint.value: Select an energy level or change the properties of the well to begin exploring.

screenButtonsHelpText.value: Explore how proximity of a second potential well impacts bound states.

energyDiagram.value:
In the Energy Diagram, observe the energy levels of two closely spaced potential wells,
a simple model of a two-atom molecule. Drag the handles change the shape of the wells, and explore 
how the energy levels and states respond as the wells move together or apart. Change the potential 
well type to explore a different two-well shape.

quantumStateGraph.value:
In the Quantum State Graph, you can observe the probability density or wave function for the 
selected energy level. If viewing the wave function, you can toggle parts of the graph, such
as the real or imaginary part, the magnitude, and, if enabled, the phase.

controlArea.value:
There are tools for inspecting the graphs and options for controlling the speed of the
simulation. Toggle the value labels on the Energy Diagram. Add a Reference Line to compare
the graphs to the boundaries of the wells. A Magnifier can aid in telling apart closely 
spaced energy levels. You can track the time the system has been evolving or hide it.
There are controls to pause, step through, or restart the system. For slowly evolving states,
you can increase the sim speed.

interactionHint.value: Select an energy level or change the properties of the wells to begin exploring.

screenButtonsHelpText.value: Explore how multiple closely-spaced potential wells influence bound states.

energyDiagram.value:
In the Energy Diagram, observe how a row of identical wells changes the energy level structure. 
Drag the handles on the curve to change all the potential wells sizes or the separation between wells. 
Change the number of wells and explore how the energy levels respond as the lattice grows. Apply an
electric field and explore its effect on the energy levels. Change the potential well type to
explore the effects of shape.

quantumStateGraph.value:
In the Quantum State Graph, you can observe the probability density or wave function for the
selected energy level, or the average probability density across a whole band.

controlArea.value:
There are controls for building the lattice and for controlling the speed of the simulation.
Set the number of wells in the lattice and apply an electric field. Toggle the value labels
on the Energy Diagram, add a Reference Line, and add a Magnifier, which is especially handy
for telling apart closely spaced energy levels. Zoom the energy axis in or out. You can track
the time the system has been evolving or hide it. There are controls to pause, step through,
or restart the system. For slowly evolving states, you can increase the sim speed.

electricField.value: Electric field set to { $electricField } volts per nanometer.

interactionHint.value: Select an energy level, change the properties of the wells, or change the number of wells to begin exploring.

screenButtonsHelpText.value: Explore superposition states and their time-dependent behavior for various potentials.

energyDiagram.value:
In the Energy Diagram, observe the energy levels of the chosen potential. The levels that
contribute to the current superposition are emphasized in proportion to their weight. Change
the potential well type to explore a different shape.

quantumStateGraph.value:
In the Quantum State Graph, you can observe the probability density or wave function for the
current superposition state. Press Play to explore how this state changes over time. Open the
Details to view the full equation along with the magnitude and phase of each contributing level.

controlArea.value:
There are controls for building superpositions and for controlling the speed of the simulation.
Switch between curated Preset superposition states or set your own Custom combinations. Open Customize
to set the magnitude and phase of each level. Toggle the value labels on the Energy Diagram,
add a Reference Line, and add a Magnifier. You can track the time the system has been evolving
or hide it. There are controls to pause, step through, or restart the system. For slowly
evolving states, you can increase the sim speed.

accessibleParagraph.value:
The Probability Density graph shows the probability density across the well for energy level { $energyLevelIndex }.
The curve has { $numberOfNodes ->
  [one] { $numberOfNodes } node.
 *[other] { $numberOfNodes } nodes.
 }
 Listen to the shape with sonification, or move the Reference Line to read the potential value at any position.

The Wave Function graph shows the real, imaginary, and magnitude parts of the wave function
across the well for energy level { $energyLevelIndex }. Listen to each part with sonification, move the
Reference Line to read values, and play time to explore how the parts behave.
